newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUG 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian cricket team will create history if they defeat England in the Ashes match to be played at Trent Bridge. If Australia wins it would mean they would hold a three-one series lead and they would be the first side to obtain a fifth successive sries win over England. Page 20

Leaders of the two rival rugby league organisations, Super League and Australian Rugby League came to a decision last night to return to a single-competition next year, this decision finally puts to an end the 30-month dispute. The hard part is now is to win support for the proposal from the clubs. Page 20

Australian Boomers basketball player Tony Ronaldson may be about to play in the National Basketball Association in the United States, after a talent scout expressed interest in him. The Vancouver Grizzlies is monitoring Ronaldson's progress. Page 18
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia is beginning to show a winning streak at yachting's Admiral's Cup in Cowes Ragamuffin team chief and owner Syd Fisher won the award for the best boat of the day. In Tuesday's Mumm Trophy contest Fisher also won his weight in champagne after two hird-place finishes. Page 47

A new inquiry has been established by Soccer Australia to investigate the trouble caused at the preliminary final against South Melbourne by Sydney United fans at Parramatta Stadium in May. The inquiry has been established in an attempt to keep the matterout of court so legal action does not interfere with the start of the Ericsson Cup. Page 47

In a rare situation at the Fairfax Printers Handicap horse racing 1,200m event at Canterbury yesterday jockey Craig Carmody was chasing his fiancee Carolyn Mason. It was the first time Mason has defeated Carmody and she will be cooking dinner for him. Page 47
THE AGE

Australian Football League club Carlton forward Luke O'Sullivan was charged yesterday with striking Adelaide's Trent Ormond-Allen with an elbow to the face at last Sunday's game at Football Park. The Australian Football league handed down the decision folowing an investigation by Officer Roger Berryman. O'Sullivan will appear before the tribunal tonight. Page B8

At Oregon Golf Club, Portland yesterday Australian golfer Greg Norman and American Brad Faxon won their third straight Fred Meter Challenge golf title. Playing alternate shots they won with a record 19-under-par total, fellow Australian Steve Elkington an his partner Craig Stadler came third at 15 under. Page B8

The further down the ranks Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor slips the further up the ladder his team players climb. Taylor's Test average is below 42, while his team mates are set to beat records. Page B8
THE HERALD SUN

Australian runner Cathy Freeman has become the interest of the international media, claiming that gold is great but her priorities lie with her family. A Moroccan reporter suggested she looked sad after her win, Freeman said she was not sure she had actually won. Page 80

Australian Football League Club Hawthorn will continue to fight for Waverley Park as an Australian Football League venue despite a plan to play no more games there after the year 2000. Australian Football League chief executive officer Wayne Jackson, Hawtorn officials and representatives from 10 local councils who want the park retained met yesterday. Page 85

Young Victorian bike rider Robert Tighello won yesterday's Tour of the Goldfields race which began in Bendigo. The 22 year-old rider escaped a 20-rider fall that injured some riders, injuries ranged from broken collarbones to cuts and bruises. Page 85
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Australian Waratahs rugby union team defeated the Japanese A team 91-21 at Sydney University Oval yesterday. The team was not disheartened by the Waratah's 62-0 lead at half time, all they wanted to do was score a try and they did in the second half. age 94

Australian Tennis Davis Cup hope Mark Philippoussis lost in straight sets 7-6, 7-5, 6-3 to Dutchman Sjeng Schalken in Ohio yesterday at the A$3m ATP championships. Team mate Mark Woodforde also went out to Andre Medvedev of Ukraine. Page 93

The Australian rugby union chairman of selectors Paul McLean is still defending the choice of Tim Horan over David Knox in the fly-half position. It has been said Horan lacks the instinctive passing and kicking skills therefore he would never be a true inernational No 10 rugby union player. Page 85
